ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r3.claim: Continual remembrance is essential to spiritual life: forgetting God leaves the soul lifeless, while remembrance keeps the heart alive.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r3.anchor: his soul becomes lifeless. It is

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r4.claim: Calling people to religion and reflecting on God’s inward and outward signs are remembrance; reflection makes it meaningful, while remembrance without reflection is only tongue exercise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r4.anchor: remembrance becomes merely an exercise of the tongue

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r1.claim: To cope with rejection and hurt, the Prophet should withdraw from those who reject truth, seek God’s mercy, and remember His name so God envelops him in mercy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r1.anchor: on such occasions, he should cut himself off from people who do not value the truth and seek refuge with the mercy of his Lord

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r2.claim: Keeping knowledge of God’s attributes fresh fortifies the believer against Satan, making him firm as a mountain.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r3.claim: Weak comprehension of divine attributes makes belief baseless or weak and leaves the believer vulnerable to every crisis.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p23/r3.anchor: every outbreak of lightning striking his own shelter

QUSHAYRI:v3p360/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p360/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p360/r6.claim: Tabattul means complete devotion and severance toward God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p309/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p309/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p309/r2.claim: Tabattul means to devote oneself exclusively; the lexical family includes separation, a woman abstaining from men, and withdrawal from marriage or society for worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p309/r2.anchor: والتبتل: ترك النكاح والزهد فيه، ومنه قول امرئ القيس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord’s name means affirming His oneness and magnifying Him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain تبتل as sincere devotion to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: أخلص إليه إخلاصا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says تبتل means striving diligently.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says it means freeing oneself for worship.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r5.speaker: سفيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r5.claim: Sufyan interprets the command as trusting God completely.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says تبتل is renouncing the world and seeking what is with God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r6.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم: التبتل رفض الدنيا وما فيها والتماس ما عند الله تعالى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r7.claim: The word’s root sense is cutting off; the command means to devote oneself wholly to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r7.anchor: وهو الأصل في الباب، يقال: تبتلت الشيء أي: قطعته

NAHHAS:v5p57/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p57/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p57/r2.claim: Tabtīlan is the verbal noun of battala because it has the same meaning as tabattala.
NAHHAS:v5p57/r2.anchor: تبتيل مصدر بتل لأن المعنى واحد وقد تبتل تبتلا

TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r4.claim: Several reports interpret devoted turning to God as raising the hands in prayer; Abu Basir describes it as lifting one's hands with supplication.
TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r4.anchor: وروى محمد بن مسلم وزرارة وحمران عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام أن التبتل هذا رفع اليدين في الصلاة

TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r5.claim: Other reported interpretations of devoted turning mention raising the hands while moving the index fingers, gesturing with a finger, or supplicating while pointing one finger.
TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r5.anchor: وفي رواية هو رفع اليدين وتحريك السبابتين، وفي رواية الإيماء بالإصبع

TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r6.claim: The hand-raising interpretations correspond to the qunut of prayer.

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r18.claim: Remembering the Lord includes glorification, takbīr, praise, affirmation of unity, prayer, Qurʾān recitation, teaching, exhortation, and guidance throughout night and day.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r18.anchor: tesbih ve tehlil, tekbir, temcid, tevhid, namaz, Kur’an okumak, ilim tâlimi, Allah için nasihat ve irşad

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r19.claim: Tabattul means withdrawing from other concerns and turning wholly to God in sincere obedience, without letting worldly pursuits occupy the heart.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r19.anchor: kendini her şeyden çekerek Rabbine çekil, ihlâs ile O’nun emr ü tâatine meşgul ol

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r20.claim: Tabattul literally involves cutting oneself off; Maryam was called Batūl for devotion, and a woman uninterested in men could also be called Batūl.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r20.anchor: ibadette Allah’a inkıtâ‘ından dolayı Hazret-i Meryem’e “Betûl” denilmiştir.

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r21.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r21.claim: Rāzī explains the wording as naming the ultimate goal, tabattul, before its necessary means, tabtīl: one must first sever worldly attachments to attain devotion to God.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r21.anchor: Evvelâ, maksûdun bizzat olan tebettülü sonra da onun şartı olan tebtîli zikreylemiştir.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.claim: تبتل إليه تبتيلا uses a verbal noun on a different pattern because تبتل has the same meaning as بتل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.anchor: فكأنه قال بتل وزعموا أن في

SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r1.claim: تبتيلا is a verbal noun on a different pattern from تبتل, used in place of its expected source; the poem similarly uses انطواء for a form on the تفعّل pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r1.anchor: مصدر على غير الصدر وهو واقع موقع التبتل؛ لأن مصدر تفعل نحو: تصرف تصرفا

SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says تبتل means بتل نفسه, so تبتيلا reflects its sense and preserves the verse endings.
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r2.anchor: لأن معنى تبتل: " بتل نفسه، فجيء به على معناه مراعاة لحق الفواصل

SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r3.claim: Tabattul means withdrawal or severance; a batul woman is separated from marriage, and batala means cut a rope.
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r3.anchor: والتبتل: الانقطاع. ومنه " امرأة بتول " ، أي: انقطعت عن النكاح، وبتلت الحبل: قطعته

SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r4.speaker: الليث
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r4.claim: Al-Layth defines batl as separating one thing from another; بتلة describes a final divorce or gift cut off from its giver.
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r4.anchor: قال الليث: البتل: تمييز الشيء من الشيء. وقالوا: " طلقة بتلة " ، و " هبة بتلة

SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r5.claim: Here the command means devote oneself to God's worship, not abandon marriage; the cited Prophetic prohibition of تبَتُّل means withdrawing from marriage.
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r5.anchor: والمراد به في الآية الكريمة الانقطاع إلى عبادة الله تعالى دون ترك النكاح

SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r6.speaker: النبي
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r6.claim: A hadith reports that the Prophet forbade تبَتُّل, meaning abstention from marriage.
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث: " أنه نهى عن التبتل " ، أي: الانقطاع عن النكاح

SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r7.claim: A monk is called متبتل because he has withdrawn from marriage; Imru al-Qays uses the word in a poetic simile.
SAMIN-DURR:73:8/r7.anchor: ومنه سمي الراهب " متبتلا " لانقطاعه عن النكاح. قال امرؤ القيس

ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r8.claim: If some night worship is missed, the day offers free time.
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r8.anchor: أي إن فاتك شيء من الليل فلك في النهار فراغ.

ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r9.claim: The command to remember the Lord is explained as remembering Him during the day.
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r9.anchor: المعنى واذكر اسم ربك بالنهار، ومعنى (وتبتل إليه)

ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r10.claim: Tabattul means devoting oneself to God in worship; Mary is called al-Batūl for her devotion, and charity is severed from its donor's wealth for God's paths.
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r10.anchor: ومعنى (وتبتل إليه) انقطع إليه في العبادة ومن هذا قيل لمريم عليها السلام البتول لأنها انقطعت إلى الله جل ثناؤه في العبادة

ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r11.claim: The verbal noun tabtīlan follows the sense of tabattala and battala rather than the expected verbal noun pattern.
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r11.anchor: والأصل في المصدر في تبتل تبتلت تبتيلا، وبتلت تبتيلا، فتبتيلا محمول على معنى تبتل إليه تبتيلا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p325/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p325/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p325/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses devotion to God as making one's supplication and worship sincere for Him alone.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p325/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وتبتل إليه تبتيلا ﴾ قال أخلص له الدعوة والعبادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r4.claim: Remembering the Lord's name means continuing in His remembrance and includes every form of dhikr, such as glorification and tahlil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r4.anchor: واذكر اسم ربك: أي دم على ذكره، وهو يتناول كل ذكر من تسبيح وتهليل وغيرهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r5.claim: Tabtīlan is a verbal noun unlike the verb's own form; its use is apt because it closes the verse's end-rhyme.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r5.anchor: وانتصب تبتيلا على أنه مصدر على غير الصدر، وحسن ذلك كونه فاصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r1.claim: Remember God continually by night and day through any form of devotion, including glorification, praise, prayer, and Qur'an recitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r1.anchor: أي ودم على ذكره تعالى ليلا ونهارا على أي وجه كان من تسبيح وتهليل وتحميد وصلاة وقراءة قرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r2.claim: The command means customary continuity, not literal uninterrupted remembrance; the Prophet had never been without remembrance, and context generalizes after specifying night and day.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r2.anchor: وفسر الأمر بالدوام لأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم ينسبه تعالى حتى يؤمر بذكره سبحانه والمراد الدوام العرفي لا الحقيقي لعدم إمكانه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r3.claim: Cut yourself off for God in worship, detach from all else, and become absorbed in awareness of Him; this turns from outward practice to the inward state.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r3.anchor: أي وانقطع إليه تعالى بالعبادة وجرد نفسك عما سواه عز وجل واستغرق في مراقبته سبحانه وكان هذا أمر بما يتعلق بالباطن بعد الأمر بما يتعلق بالظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r4.claim: Tabtīlan is accusative because tabattal includes the sense of battala.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r4.anchor: ونصبه بتبتل لتضمنه معنى بتل على ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r5.claim: The wording also attends to the verse-ending cadence.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r5.anchor: وكيفما كان الأمر ففيه مراعاة الفواصل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r6.claim: The author points back to his discussion of anbattakum min al-arḍ nabātan.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p106/r6.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام في تحقيق ذلك عند قوله تعالى والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r3.claim: Remember God continually by night and day; remembrance includes glorification, declaring unity, praise, prayer, Qurʾān recitation, and studying knowledge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r3.anchor: ودم على ذكره ليلا ونهارا، وذكر الله يتناول كل ما يذكر به

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r4.claim: Devote yourself to Him in worship and detach yourself from all else.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r4.anchor: وانقطع إليه بالعبادة وجرد نفسك عما سواه

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r5.claim: The verbal noun tabtīlan replaces the expected tabattulan for its allusive force and to preserve the verse endings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r5.anchor: ولهذه الرمزة ومراعاة الفواصل وضعه موضع تبتلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r4.claim: Remember God by every form of remembrance, including praise, submission, prayer, recitation, supplication, and pursuing religious learning and proper conduct; persist in it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r4.anchor: بكل ما يكون ذكرا من اسم وصفة وثناء وخضوع وتسبيح وتحميد وصلاة وقراءة ودعاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r5.claim: Magnifying God's name magnifies the One named through monotheism and sincerity, helping the servant in both the present and future lives.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r5.anchor: فإذا عظمت الاسم بالذكر فقد عظمت المسمى بالتوحيد والإخلاص , وذلك عون لك على مصالح الدارين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r6.claim: When Fatima asked for a servant to spare her fatigue, the Prophet directed her to glorify, praise, and magnify God at bedtime.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r6.anchor: أرشد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أعز الخلق عليه فاطمة ابنته رضي الله عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r7.claim: Tabattul means progressively cutting oneself off from distractions and making all acts sincere for God until detachment becomes a settled disposition.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r7.anchor: اجتهد في قطع نفسك عن كل شاغل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r8.claim: The root batl means cutting; a batlah charity is separated from its giver.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam defines tabattul as rejecting the world and seeking what is with God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r9.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم : التبتل رفض الدنيا وما فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r10.claim: Maryam is called al-Batul for turning away from all creation toward God; Fatima is likewise called al-Batul as cut off from any peer or equal.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r10.anchor: والبتول مريم عليها السلام لانقطاعها إلى الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r11.claim: The verse calls for the stance of the testimony of divine unity: turn to God, turn away from all else, persist in remembrance, and cast off desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r11.anchor: فالمراد بهذا هو المراد بكلمة التوحيد المقتضية للإقبال عليه والإعراض عن كل ما سواه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r12.claim: The paired forms create rhetorical completion: the verb tabattul implies an omitted verbal noun, while tabtīlan implies an omitted verb, stressing effort and difficulty.

DURR-FULL:v8p317/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains devotion to God as sincere dedication to Him.
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r6.anchor: وفي قوله: {وتبتل إليه تبتيلا} قال: أخلص لله إخلاصا

DURR-FULL:v8p317/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r10.claim: Qatada defines daytime as a long free span and devotion as giving God supplication and worship exclusively.
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r10.anchor: عن قتادة {سبحا طويلا} قال: فراغا طويلا {وتبتل إليه تبتيلا} قال: أخلص له الدعوة والعبادة

DURR-FULL:v8p317/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r11.claim: Mujahid says to devote supplication and prayer to God sincerely.
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد {وتبتل إليه تبتيلا} قال: أخلص له المسألة والدعاء إخلاصا

DURR-FULL:v8p317/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r12.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says to devote oneself sincerely to God.
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r12.anchor: عن الحسن {وتبتل إليه تبتيلا} قال: أخلص له إخلاصا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r1.claim: The command to remember is coordinated with the night-prayer command, but its unqualified time extends it to night and day, as in 76:25.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r1.anchor: عطف على { قم الليل } ( المزمل : 2 ) وقصد بإطلاق الأمر عن تعيين زمان إلى إفادة تعميمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r2.claim: “Name” is included because the commanded remembrance is verbal, while spoken words encompass inward thought since speech follows what is in the mind; compare 7:205.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r2.anchor: وإقحام كلمة { اسم } لأن المأمور به ذكر اللسان وهو جامع للتذكر بالعقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r3.claim: Tabattul is separation: grammatically the reflexive of battala, figuratively intensified as if another caused it; here it means turning thought toward what pleases God, away from people. Imruʾ al-Qays's “منارة ممسى راهب متبتل” illustrates the usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r3.anchor: والتبتل : شدة البتل ، وهو مصدر تبتل القاصر الذي هو مطاوع بتله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r4.claim: Tabtil is the verbal noun of transitive form battala; using it instead of tabattul signals that separation entails actively cutting oneself off from all but God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r4.anchor: والتبتيل : مصدر بتل المشدد الذي هو فعل متعد مثل التقطيع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r5.claim: The paired forms portray training the self in detachment, and tabtil also preserves the cadence of the surrounding verse endings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r5.anchor: فالجمع بين { تبتل } و { تبتيلا } مشير إلى إراضة النفس على ذلك التبتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r6.claim: The commanded separation is limited to activities that obstruct night prayer or daytime preaching and disputation; ordinary food, sleep, family, marriage, and perfume can all serve God's religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r6.anchor: والمراد بالانقطاع المأمور به انقطاع خاص وهو الانقطاع عن الأعمال التي تمنعه من قيام الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r7.claim: The Prophet said that women and perfume had been made beloved to him from worldly things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r7.anchor: وقد قال : ( حبب إلي من دنياكم النساء والطيب )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r1.claim: The command does not mean monastic withdrawal from women and managing life, which is incompatible with the Prophet's messenger role.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r1.anchor: وليس هو التبتل المفضي إلى الرهبانية وهو الإعراض عن النساء وعن تدبير أمور الحياة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r2.claim: In a report in the Sahih, the Prophet rejected ʿUthman ibn Mazʿun's request to withdraw from women; he said that had he permitted it, they would have castrated themselves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r2.anchor: وفي حديث سعد في ( الصحيح ) ( رد رسول الله على عثمان بن مظعون التبتل ولو أذن له لاختصينا )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r3.claim: The greatest devotion is renouncing associationism, the meaning of hanifiyya; this explains the following affirmation that God alone is deity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r3.anchor: ومن أكبر التبتل إلى الله الانقطاع عن الإشراك ، وهو معنى الحنيفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r4.claim: The Prophet should continually worship, remain mindful of God, and devote himself to preaching; the command renews his existing practice, guided first through tahannuth at Hira and then revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r4.anchor: وخلاصة المعنى : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مأمور أن لا تخلو أوقاته عن إقبال على عبادة الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r5.claim: The earlier al-Qalam (68:51) already described the disbelievers nearly tripping the Prophet with their eyes when hearing the Reminder; early suras mostly set duties particular to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p266/r5.anchor: فإن في سورة القلم ( وقد نزلت قبل المزمل ) { وإن يكاد الذين كفروا ليزلقونك بأبصارهم لما سمعوا الذكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r1.claim: Remember your Lord’s name during the day as well.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى واذكر اسم ربك أي بالنهار أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses tabattal as devoting oneself sincerely to God.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the verb as turning exclusively to God, from a root meaning to cut off.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة انقطع إليه من قولك بثلت الشيء إذا قطعته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses it as devoting oneself to worship; Mary is called al-Batul for her devotion, and a batlah charity is separated from the donor’s wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج انقطع إليه في العبادة ومنه قيل لمريم البتول لأنها انقطعت إلى الله تعالى في العبادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r5.claim: The expected verbal noun is tabattulan; tabtilan is used here according to the meaning of tabattala.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392#2/r5.anchor: والأصل في مصدر تبتل تبتلا وإنما قوله تعالى تبتيلا محمول على معنى تبتل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r1.claim: Remember God often, devote yourself to Him, and turn to worship when worldly tasks and needs are finished; Ibn Kathir connects this to 94:7 and cites Ibn Zayd in similar terms.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r1.anchor: أكثر من ذكره، وانقطع إليه، وتفرغ لعبادته إذا فرغت من أشغالك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأبو صالح، وعطية، والضحاك، والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r2.claim: These authorities explain the command as making worship sincerely and exclusively for God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد، وأبو صالح، وعطية، والضحاك، والسدي: {وتبتل إليه تبتيلا} أي: أخلص له العبادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r3.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the phrase as striving and devoting oneself to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: اجتهد وبتل إليه نفسك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir notes that a worshipper is called a متبتل; the related hadith prohibition of تبتل means withdrawing to worship and abandoning marriage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p255/r4.anchor: يقال للعابد: متبتل، ومنه الحديث المروي: أنه نهى عن التبتل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r1.claim: Remember God continually by night and day and pursue every good form of remembrance: glorification, declarations of unity and greatness, prayer, Qurʾān recitation, study, and more; the Messenger filled his time with it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r1.anchor: ودم على ذكره في ليلك ونهارك ، واحرص عليه ، وذكر الله يتناول كل ما كان من ذكر طيب : تسبيح ، وتهليل ، وتكبير ، وتمجيد ، وتوحيد ، وصلاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r2.claim: Tabattal ilayhi means detach yourself and devote yourself to God.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r3.claim: Tabtīlan stands where tabattulan might be expected because tabattala means “detach oneself”; the wording follows that meaning and preserves the verse endings.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#3/r3.anchor: لأن معنى تبتل بتل نفسه ، فجيء به على معناه مراعاة لحق الفواصل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r28.claim: Al-Mawardi says to direct one's work toward the Lord's face.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r29.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r29.claim: Ibn Baḥr says that when beginning recitation, one should start with “In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r29.anchor: أنه إذا أردت القراءة فابدأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم , قاله ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r30.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r30.claim: Al-Mawardi also allows remembering God's promise and warning so as to obey Him and avoid disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r30.anchor: واذكر اسم ربك في وعده ووعيده لتتوفر على طاعته وتعدل عن معصيته

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r31.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r31.claim: Mujahid glosses tabattul as sincere devotion to God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r32.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r32.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r32.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses it as worshipping God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r32.anchor: تعبد له تعبدا , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r33.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r33.speaker: أبو جعفر الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r33.claim: Abu Jaʿfar al-Tabari says it means turning wholly to God; Maryam is called al-Batul for her devotion, though a hadith warns against withdrawing from people and communal life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r33.anchor: انقطع إليه انقطاعا , قاله أبو جعفر الطبري , ومنه مريم البتول لانقطاعها إلى الله تعالى , وجاء في الحديث النهي عن التبتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r34.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r34.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r34.claim: Al-Mawardi also allows the sense of supplicating humbly.

MUJAHID:v2p700/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p700/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p700/r1.claim: Mujahid explains devotion to God as giving oneself to Him sincerely.
MUJAHID:v2p700/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وتبتل إليه تبتيلا ﴾ يقول أخلص إليه إخلاصا

BURSEVI:v10p162/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162/r6.claim: Remember God continually, by glorification, declaration of unity, praise, prayer, Quran recitation, or studying knowledge; especially remember after dawn and before sunset, times of opening and grace.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r6.anchor: ودم على ذكره تعالى ليلا ونهارا على أي وجه كان من تسبيح وتهليل وتحميد وصلاة وقراءة قرآن ودراسة علم

BURSEVI:v10p162/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162/r7.claim: Constant remembrance is a duty of those brought near, whether by heart, tongue, or limbs, and whether standing, sitting, or reclining.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r7.anchor: وذكر الله على الدوام من وظائف المقربين سواء كان قلبا أو لسانا أو أركانا وسواء كان قياما أو قعودا أو على النوب

BURSEVI:v10p162/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p162/r8.claim: The Prophet reports that whoever enumerates God's beautiful names enters Paradise; the author takes naming God as a means of remembering Him.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r8.anchor: قال عليه السلام من أحصاها أي حصلها دخل الجنة فالمراد من ذكر اسمه فذكره تعالى بواسطة ذكر اسمه

BURSEVI:v10p162/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162/r9.claim: He links remembrance through God's name to the command to remember one's Lord when one forgets, since remembrance and forgetting are states of the heart.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r9.anchor: قال تعالى : {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت} فالذكر والنسيان في الحقيقة

BURSEVI:v10p162/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162/r10.claim: When the Remembered manifests, remembrance and the rememberer vanish.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r10.anchor: وعند تجلى المذكور يفنى الذكر والذاكر كما قال شيخي وسندي روح الله روحه

BURSEVI:v10p162/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r11.speaker: شيخي وسندي
BURSEVI:v10p162/r11.claim: The author's shaykh teaches that persistent, divinely enabled attention to a metaphorical name creates an affinity with that name's secret and spirit, in proportion to the effort.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r11.anchor: من اشتغل من الأسماء المجازية بما يسر الله الاشتغال به وداوم عليه فلا ريب إنه يحصل بينه وبين سر هذا الاسم

BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r1.claim: As affinity with a name grows through sustained effort, the true divine name relates to the servant by God's gift; as impurity recedes, God manifests through that name according to the servant's readiness and grants spiritual and cosmic knowledge, directly, through ordered intermediaries, or both.
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r1.anchor: بينهما وكملت بحسب قوة الاشتغال وكماله

BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r2.claim: Some say one should say 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' before Quran recitation or prayer.
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم في الآية إذا أردت قراءة القرآن أو الصلاة فقل بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r3.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r3.claim: Al-Qashani reads 'the name of your Lord' as your own self: know and remember yourself lest God leave you forgotten, and strive to perfect yourself after knowing your reality.
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r3.anchor: وقال القاشاني واذكر اسم ربك الذي هو أنت أي اعرف نفسك واذكرها ولا تنسها فينساك الله

BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r4.claim: Tabattul means detachment; the command is to turn completely to God through worship, sincerity, and undivided orientation.
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى وانقطع إلى ربك انقطاعا تاما بالعبادة وإخلاص والية

BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r5.claim: Complete devotion means stripping the self of thoughts of everything besides God, as in the linked command, 'Say: God, then leave them.'
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r5.anchor: كما قال تعالى : قل الله ثم ذرهم وبالفارسية

BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r6.claim: This detachment does not conflict with the prohibition of monasticism or celibacy: the hadith's tabattul means abandoning marriage, which scripture and the Prophet encourage.
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r6.anchor: وليس هذا منافيا لقوله عليه السلام لا رهبانية ولا تبتل في الإسلام فإن التبتل هنا هو الانقطاع عن النكاح

BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r7.claim: Maryam is called al-Batul for abstaining from men, while Fatima's title reflects detachment from everything besides God, not from marriage.
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r7.anchor: وأما إطلاق البتول على فاطمة الزهراء رضي الله عنها فلكونها شبيهة بسيدة نساء بني إسرائيل في الانقطاع عما سوى الله

BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r8.claim: Some explain the intensive verbal noun tabtīlan in place of tabattulan by its sense, 'he detached himself,' maintaining the Quran's superior word order and sound arrangement.
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r8.anchor: وقيل تبتلا مكان تتتلا لأن معنى تبتل بتل نفسه

BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r9.claim: The form also signals that complete detachment is God's act: the servant's effort is enabled by God, who detaches him from all else.
BURSEVI:v10p162#2/r9.anchor: فإن التبتيل فعل الله فلا يحصل للعبد إلا بمعاونته

MUQATIL:73:7-11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:7-11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:7-11/r2.claim: Remembering the Lord's name means affirming his oneness and sincerity.
MUQATIL:73:7-11/r2.anchor: { واذكر اسم ربك } يعني بالتوحيد والإخلاص

MUQATIL:73:7-11/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:7-11/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:7-11/r3.claim: Devotion means sincere dedication to God in supplication and worship.
MUQATIL:73:7-11/r3.anchor: { وتبتل إليه تبتيلا } [آية: 8] يعني وأخلص إليه إخلاصا في الدعاء والعبادة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r1.claim: Persist in remembering God day and night; remembrance includes glorification, declarations of unity and greatness, prayer, Qurʾān recitation, and study.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r1.anchor: ودم على ذكره في الليل والنهار وذكر الله يتناول التسبيح والتهليل والتكبير والصلاة وتلاوة القرآن ودراسة العلم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r2.claim: Tabattul means withdrawing from everything for worship and turning to God alone, hoping for good from Him and no one else.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r2.anchor: انقطع إلى عبادته عن كل شيء والتبتل الانقطاع إلى الله تعالى بتأميل الخير منه دون غيره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r3.claim: Another view takes it as renouncing the world and seeking what is with God.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r3.anchor: وقيل رفض الدنيا وما فيها والتماس ما عند الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r4.claim: The non-matching verbal noun adds emphasis; it may also be chosen to preserve the verse-end rhyme.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#2/r4.anchor: في اختلاف المصدر زيادة تأكيد أي بتلك الله فتبتل أوجئ به مراعاة لحق الفواصل

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r1.claim: Remember the Lord by calling on His beautiful names, so that prayer yields a praiseworthy outcome; another view says to direct one’s work toward God’s approval.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r1.anchor: أي ادعه بأسمائه الحسنى، ليحصل لك مع الصلاة محمود العاقبة. وقيل: أي اقصد بعملك وجه ربك.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r2.speaker: سهل
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r2.claim: Sahl says to recite “In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate” at the start of prayer; its blessing connects the worshipper to God and cuts him off from all else.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r2.anchor: وقال سهل: اقرأ باسم الله الرحمن الرحيم في ابتداء صلاتك توصلك بركة قراءتها إلى ربك،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r3.claim: Another view is to remember God’s promises and threats, obeying Him and avoiding disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r3.anchor: وقيل: اذكر اسم ربك في وعده ووعيده لتوفر على طاعته وتعدل عن معصيته.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r4.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets the command as praying to the Lord during daytime; al-Qurṭubī approves this as a pairing with the preceding mention of night.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: صل لربك أي بالنهار. قلت: وهذا حسن فإنه لما ذكر الليل ذكر النهار إذ هو قسيمه

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r5.claim: The night-day pairing recalls 25:62, where God makes night and day alternate for anyone wishing to remember.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r5.anchor: وهو الذي جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن أراد أن يذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r6.claim: Tabattul means devoting oneself exclusively to God in worship and associating no one with Him; its root denotes cutting off, as in irrevocable divorce or charity and Maryam al-Batūl’s dedication.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r6.anchor: التبتل: الانقطاع إلى عبادة الله عز وجل أي انقطع بعبادتك إليه، ولا تشرك به غيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r7.speaker: ابن عرفة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r7.claim: Ibn ʿArafa says the word’s original Arabic sense is solitude; al-Qurṭubī considers devotion to worship the stronger reading in context.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن أصله عند العرب التفرد قاله ابن عرفة. والأول أقوى لما ذكرنا.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r8.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r8.claim: A Prophetic report prohibits tabattul understood as withdrawing from people and communal gatherings.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث النهي عن التبتل، وهو الانقطاع عن الناس والجماعات.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r9.claim: The verbal noun tabtīlan instead of tabattulan reflects the sense “he cut himself off,” while also preserving the verse’s rhyme endings.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r9.anchor: لأن معنى تبتل بتل نفسه، فجيء به على معناه مراعاة لحق الفواصل.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r10.claim: Al-Qurṭubī refers to 5:87’s discussion of disliking ascetic renunciation of lawful pleasures and monasticism.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r10.anchor: قد مضي في «المائدة» في تفسير قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r11.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r11.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says that in a corrupt age, with weakened trust and widespread unlawful wealth, isolation is better than social mixing and celibacy better than marriage.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r11.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وأما اليوم وقد مرجت عهود الناس، وخفت أماناتهم، واستولى الحرام على الحطام، فالعزلة خير

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r12.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī clarifies that the verse means separation from idols and worship besides God; Mujāhid says it means worshipping God sincerely, not monastic renunciation.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r12.anchor: وكذلك قال مجاهد: معناه: أخلص له العبادة، ولم يرد التبتل، فصار التبتل مأمورا به في القرآن،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r13.claim: The Qurʾānic command to devote worship sincerely differs from the Sunnah’s prohibition of Christian-style renunciation of marriage and retreat to monasteries, so the texts do not conflict; 98:5 gives the parallel command to worship sincerely.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8/r13.anchor: فالتبتل المأمور به: الانقطاع إلى الله بإخلاص العبادة كما قال تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:73:8#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8#2/r1.claim: The commanded devotion is sincere worship of God, while the prohibited tabattul is Christian-like avoidance of marriage and monastic retreat; in times of religious turmoil, a Muslim may best protect faith by tending sheep in remote mountain pastures.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:8#2/r1.anchor: والتبتل المنهي عنه: هو سلوك مسلك النصارى في ترك النكاح والترهب في الصوامع، لكن عند فساد الزمان

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r5.claim: The sequence first orders night vigil, explains why night rather than day, then identifies remembrance and devotion as the noblest acts during that vigil.

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r1.claim: The verse commands two things: remembrance and tabattul, or complete turning toward God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r1.anchor: وهذه الآية تدل على أنه تعالى أمر بشيئين أحدهما : الذكر ، والثاني : التبتل

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r2.claim: Uttering God's name is the first stage: after some time the name falls away while the Named remains; the next stage is inward remembrance in 7:205.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r2.anchor: والمرتبة الثانية هي المراد بقوله في السورة الأخرى

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r3.claim: Remembrance of the Lord first entails contemplating lordship, God's nurturing and beneficence; attention to favors occupies the heart, so it is not yet wholly absorbed in God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r3.anchor: وربوبيته عبارة عن أنواع تربيته لك وإحسانه إليك

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r4.claim: The ascent then reaches remembrance of divinity, linked to 2:200; this station brings awe because divinity signifies irresistible might, exaltedness, and self-sufficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r4.anchor: وفي هذا المقام يكون الإنسان في مقام الهيبة والخشية

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r5.claim: The servant continues through stations of majesty, transcendence, and sanctification until reaching the unique divine identity, which language and thought cannot fully describe.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r5.anchor: ولا يزال العبد يرقى في هذا المقام مترددا في مقامات الجلال والتنزيه والتقديس

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r6.claim: The ascent ends at the One, with no likeness in attributes, no composite identity whose parts could be considered separately, and no analogy to anything perceived by the soul.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r6.anchor: لأنه ليس هناك نظير في الصفات

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r7.claim: God is manifest as the source of every manifestation yet hidden beyond created intellects; the commentary says overwhelming radiance conceals Him from reason.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#3/r7.anchor: فهي الظاهرة لأنها مبدأ ظهور كل ظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r1.claim: All exegetes gloss tabattul as sincerity; lexically, it means cutting off, as Mary is called al-Batūl for devoting herself to worship and a batlah donation is severed from its owner's wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r1.anchor: أن جميع المفسرين فسروا التبتل بالإخلاص

RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r2.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r2.claim: Al-Layth defines tabtīl as distinguishing one thing from another and batūl as a woman who withdraws from men and has no desire for them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r2.anchor: وقال الليث : التبتيل تمييز الشيء عن الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r3.claim: Al-Farra says a worshipper who abandons everything and devotes himself to worship has cut himself off from all else for God's command and obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r3.anchor: قال الفراء : يقال للعابد إذا ترك كل شيء

RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam defines tabattul as renouncing the world and everything in it while seeking what is with God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r4.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم التبتل رفض الدنيا مع كل ما فيها والتماس ما عند الله

RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r5.claim: Al-Razi says the verse demands severance from everything besides God and turning to God Himself; ordinary pursuit of afterlife, worship, or knowledge still fixes attention on an intermediary.
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r5.anchor: أي انقطع عن كل ما سواه إليه

RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r6.claim: Seeking worship for its own sake, reward, or identity as a perfect worshipper remains attachment to something other than God; seeking gnosis for itself likewise stops short.
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r6.anchor: فمن آثر العبادة لنفس العبادة أو لطلب الثواب أو ليصير متعبدا كاملا

RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r7.claim: True arrival prefers servitude for the Worshipped and knowledge for the Known; it exceeds verbal explanation and must be directly experienced rather than learned secondhand.
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r7.anchor: ومن آثر العبودية لا للعبودية بل للمعبود وآثر العرفان لا للعرفان بل للمعروف

RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r8.claim: Al-Razi compares this severance to overwhelming love, which consumes bodily powers, blinds the eyes, removes other aims, and distinguishes attachment to the beloved from attachment to seeing the beloved.
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r8.anchor: فهناك يظهر الفرق بين التبتل إلى المعشوق وبين التبتل إلى رؤية المعشوق

RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r9.claim: The expected forms would be tabattulan to Him or make yourself devoted to Him; the chosen wording makes tabattul the essential goal and tabtīl the necessary means.
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r9.anchor: الواجب أن يقال : وتبتل إليه تبتلا

RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r10.claim: Although tabtīl is only instrumental and interrupts total devotion, it must come first, as 29:69 promises guidance to those who strive for God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p157/r10.anchor: إلا أنه لا بد أولا من التبتيل حتى يحصل التبتل كما قال تعالى

STUDYQURAN:73:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r1.claim: Once believers finish their affairs, they should devote themselves to God, as in the command to exert oneself when free in 94:7.
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r1.anchor: Once believers have finished with their affairs, they should devote themselves to God, as in 94:7

STUDYQURAN:73:8/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r2.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r2.claim: Some understand remembering the Lord’s Name as reciting the basmalah at the start of Quran recitation.
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r2.anchor: Some say the command remember the Name of thy Lord means to recite the basmalah (In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful), at the beginning of Quranic recitation (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:73:8/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r3.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r3.claim: Others take the command as urging remembrance of God at every moment of every day, since God’s remembrance is greater.
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r3.anchor: others see it as an exhortation to remember God at every moment of every day (Aj), since the remembrance of God is surely greater (29:45).

STUDYQURAN:73:8/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r4.claim: Tabattal literally means to sever or cut off.
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r4.anchor: Devote translates tabattal, which literally means “to sever” or “to cut off.”

STUDYQURAN:73:8/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r5.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r5.claim: The command is interpreted as cutting oneself off from everything other than God’s remembrance.
STUDYQURAN:73:8/r5.anchor: It is thus interpreted to mean cutting oneself off from everything other than the remembrance of God (Aj).

SULAMI:v2p355#6/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r1.claim: Sahl says beginning prayer with the basmala brings the worshipper to God through its blessing and severs them from everything besides Him.
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r1.anchor: قال سهل : اقرا باسم الله الرحمن الرحيم في ابتداء صلاتك توصلك بركة قراءتها إلى ربك وتقطعك

SULAMI:v2p355#6/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r2.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r2.claim: Dhu al-Nun pictures remembrance as branches rooted in the celestial realm whose fruits feed hearts and ennoble them in both worlds; he wonders what love's assault would bring and cites a verse-poem of one consumed by longing for the One.
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r2.anchor: وقال ذو النون : سبحان من دلى من الذكر اغصانا إلى الدنيا أشجارها في الملكوت فاطعم القلوب من ثمارها

SULAMI:v2p355#6/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r3.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r3.claim: Dhu al-Nun says the knower's punishment is being cut off from remembrance.
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r3.anchor: وقال : لكل شيء عقوبة وعقوبة العارف انقطاعه عن الذكر .

SULAMI:v2p355#6/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r4.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r4.claim: Abu Uthman says one who has not tasted the loneliness of heedlessness cannot taste the intimacy of remembrance.
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r4.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : من لم يذق وحشة الغفلة لا يجد طعم أنس الذكر .

SULAMI:v2p355#6/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r5.claim: Ibn Ata interprets retreat to God as reaching Him through connection; those who return do so from the road, since none reaches Him and then turns away.
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r5.anchor: سمعت أبا القاسم البزاز يقول : قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ﴿ وتبتل إليه تبتيلا ﴾ لتصل به اتصالا وما رجع من رجع

SULAMI:v2p355#6/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r6.claim: Some describe prophetic spiritual training as progressing through discipline by commands and prohibitions, refinement through decree and power, dissolution of personal agency, and finally retreat to God.
SULAMI:v2p355#6/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : فتح على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أولا أسباب التأديب ثم أسباب التهذيب ثم أسباب التذويب

TUSTARI:73:8/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:73:8/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:73:8/r1.claim: Read 'In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful' at the opening of prayer: its blessing connects the worshipper to God and cuts them off from all else.
TUSTARI:73:8/r1.anchor: اقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم في افتتاح صلاتك توصلك بركة قراءتها إلى ربك

TABATABAI:73:7-8/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r13.claim: The commands to remember God and devote oneself to Him describe night prayer and explain the command to recite with tartil.
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r13.anchor: الظاهر أنه يصف صلاة الليل فهو كالعطف التفسيري على قوله

TABATABAI:73:7-8/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r14.claim: On this reading, remembering the Lord's name is verbal remembrance accompanied by the heart, and devotion likewise includes verbal expression.
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r14.anchor: وعلى هذا فالمراد بذكر اسم الرب تعالى الذكر اللفظي بمواطاة من القلب

TABATABAI:73:7-8/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r15.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r15.claim: An alternative generalizes the command to continuous customary remembrance day and night in any form, since the Prophet never forgot God.
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r15.anchor: وقيل الآية تعميم بعد التخصيص والمراد بالذكر دوام ذكره تعالى ليلا ونهارا على أي وجه كان

TABATABAI:73:7-8/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r16.claim: Not forgetting God does not rule out a command to remember Him verbally; not forgetting before an address does not rule out a later command.
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r16.anchor: أن عدم نسيانه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ربه إلى حين الخطاب لا ينافي أمره بذكره بعده

TABATABAI:73:7-8/r17.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r17.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r17.claim: He rejects the claim that perpetual remembrance is impossible or merely customary: God is never absent from a person, whether noticed or overlooked.
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r17.anchor: فالله جل ذكره مذكور للإنسان لا يغيب عنه ولا لحظه سواء تنبه عليه الإنسان أو غفل عنه

TABATABAI:73:8-9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r1.claim: God may make Himself known so that a person never loses awareness of Him; this state is not exclusive to angels, as 41:38 and 21:20 show.
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r1.anchor: ومن الممكن أن يعرفه الله نفسه بحيث لا يغفل عنه ولا في حال

TABATABAI:73:8-9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r2.claim: The name may mean one of God's names or specifically the name Allah.
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r2.anchor: أمر بذكر اسم من أسمائه أو لفظ الجلالة خاصة

TABATABAI:73:8-9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes the name as the basmala.

TABATABAI:73:8-9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r4.claim: The shift from first-person plural to third person may awaken awareness of servitude, the bond between servant and Lord.
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r4.anchor: وفي قوله { ربك } التفات عن التكلم مع الغير

TABATABAI:73:8-9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r5.claim: Tabattul means turning away from others and devoting oneself to God.
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r5.anchor: فسر التبتل بالانقطاع أي وانقطع إلى الله

TABATABAI:73:8-9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r6.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r6.claim: A report from the Imams of the Prophet's family explains tabattul as raising one's hands to God and beseeching Him; al-Tabataba'i finds this fitting if remembrance is verbal.
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r6.anchor: ومن المروي عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أن التبتل رفع اليد إلى الله

TABATABAI:73:8-9/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r7.claim: Tabtil is an absolute object where the expected verbal noun would be tabattul.
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r7.anchor: مفعول مطلق ظاهرا وكان مقتضى الظاهر أن يقال وتبتل إليه تبتلا

TABATABAI:73:8-9/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r8.claim: One explanation says tabattul carries the sense of batala: sever yourself completely from everything but God, or compel yourself to raise your hands and plead.

TABATABAI:73:8-9/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r9.claim: A different explanation says the form was chosen to preserve the verse endings.

TABATABAI:73:8-9/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r12.claim: Calling God Lord of the whole world prevents taking Him as the Prophet's private deity, like a pagan's personal idol, and grounds the call to monotheism.
TABATABAI:73:8-9/r12.anchor: مأمور باتخاذه ربا لأنه ربه ورب العالم كله

AKHFASH:v2p552/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p552/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p552/r3.claim: The regular masdar of تبتل is التبتل; تبتيلا is not its expected masdar, just as نبات is used in place of the masdar إنبات.
AKHFASH:v2p552/r3.anchor: وقال {وتبتل إليه تبتيلا} فلم يجيء بمصدره ومصدره "التبتل"

AKHFASH:v2p552/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p552/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p552/r4.claim: An unnamed poet’s al-Wafir line is cited in this discussion of verbal nouns; it witnesses اتباعا after تتبعه.
AKHFASH:v2p552/r4.anchor: وخير الأمر ما استقبلت منه * وليس بأن تتبعه اتباعا

TABRISI:73:1-10/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:1-10/r13.claim: Tabattul means severing oneself for God and devoting worship exclusively to Him; its root means cutting something off.
TABRISI:73:1-10/r13.anchor: والتبتل الانقطاع إلى الله عز وجل وإخلاص العبادة له

TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r13.claim: The root means cutting off; an irrevocable endowment is separated from its donor, and Mary is called al-Batūl for devotion to God.
TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r13.anchor: وأصله من تبلت الشيء قطعته وصدقة بتة بتلة أي بائنة مقطوعة

TABRISI:73:8-9/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:8-9/r11.claim: Remember God by invoking His names, through which worship is performed in supplication.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r11.anchor: يعني أسماء الله تعالى التي تعبد بالدعاء بها

TABRISI:73:8-9/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:8-9/r12.claim: One interpretation is to recite the basmala at prayer's start so its blessing connects the reciter to God and separates him from all else.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r12.anchor: اقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم في ابتداء صلاتك توصلك بركة قراءتها إلى ربك

TABRISI:73:8-9/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:8-9/r13.claim: Another interpretation is to direct one's deeds toward God's pleasure.

TABRISI:73:8-9/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
TABRISI:73:8-9/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others explain tabattul as sincere devotion in supplication and worship.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r14.anchor: أخلص له إخلاصا عن ابن عباس وغيره يعني في الدعاء والعبادة

TABRISI:73:8-9/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r15.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:73:8-9/r15.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says tabattul means turning wholly to God, the root sense.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r15.anchor: انقطع إليه انقطاعا عن عطاء وهو الأصل

TABRISI:73:8-9/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r16.speaker: شقيق
TABRISI:73:8-9/r16.claim: Shafīq explains tabattul as relying on God.

TABRISI:73:8-9/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r17.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:73:8-9/r17.claim: Ibn Zayd explains tabattul as devoting oneself to worship.

TABRISI:73:8-9/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:8-9/r18.claim: The prohibition on tabattul refers to withdrawing from people and communal gatherings; here the Prophet is to devote himself to God.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r18.anchor: والمراد به الانقطاع عن الناس والجماعات وكان يجب أن يقول تبتلا

TABRISI:73:8-9/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:8-9/r19.claim: One explanation says tabtīlan is used to match the endings of the surah's verses.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r19.anchor: إنما قال تبتيلا ليطابق أواخر آيات السورة

TABRISI:73:8-9/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r20.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
TABRISI:73:8-9/r20.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbd Allāh say tabattul here means raising the hands in prayer.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r20.anchor: أن التبتل هنا رفع اليدين في الصلاة

TABRISI:73:8-9/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r21.speaker: أبو بصير
TABRISI:73:8-9/r21.claim: Abū Baṣīr says tabattul is raising one's hands to God and beseeching Him.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r21.anchor: هو رفع يدك إلى الله وتضرعك إليه

FARRA:v3p198/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p198/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p198/r1.claim: Tabattul is sincere devotion to God: the worshipper cuts off everything else and turns to worship, keeping only God’s command and obedience.
FARRA:v3p198/r1.anchor: أخلص لله إخلاصا، ويقال للعابد إذا ترك كل شيء، وأقبل على العبادة: قد تبتل، أي: قطع كل شيء إلا أمر الله وطاعته.

THALABI:v10p62#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p62#2/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord’s name means affirming His oneness and magnifying Him.

THALABI:v10p62#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r2.speaker: سهل
THALABI:v10p62#2/r2.claim: Sahl says to recite the basmala at the beginning of prayers, joining its blessing to the Lord and cutting oneself off from all else.
THALABI:v10p62#2/r2.anchor: وقال سهل اقرأ: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم في ابتداء صلواتك

THALABI:v10p62#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p62#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most interpreters say tabattul means sincere devotion to God.
THALABI:v10p62#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأكثر الناس: أخلص إليه إخلاصا

THALABI:v10p62#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p62#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses tabattul as exerting oneself.

THALABI:v10p62#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p62#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says to devote oneself to worship.

THALABI:v10p62#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r6.speaker: شفيق
THALABI:v10p62#2/r6.claim: Shafīq interprets it as placing one’s trust in God.

THALABI:v10p62#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
THALABI:v10p62#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says it means cutting oneself off to God; the author connects the root to cutting, a severed gift, and a detached house.
THALABI:v10p62#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطاء: انقطع إليه انقطاعا، وهو الأصل في هذا الباب

THALABI:v10p62#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r8.speaker: أبو القيم
THALABI:v10p62#2/r8.claim: Abū al-Qāsim urges connection with God so complete that those who reach Him do not turn back; those who turn back never reached Him.
THALABI:v10p62#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو القيم: اتصل به اتصالا ما رجع من رجع إلا من الطريق

THALABI:v10p62#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p62#2/r9.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s description of a monk as mutabatt il attests the word’s association with withdrawal and devotion.

THALABI:v10p62#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p62#2/r10.anchor: ونهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن التبتل

THALABI:v10p62#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r11.speaker: محمد بن علي
THALABI:v10p62#2/r11.claim: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī interprets the command as raising the hands in prayer.
THALABI:v10p62#2/r11.anchor: محمد بن علي: ارفع اليدين في الصلاة

THALABI:v10p62#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62#2/r12.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v10p62#2/r12.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says tabattul is abandoning worldly things and seeking what is with God.
THALABI:v10p62#2/r12.anchor: زيد بن أسلم: التبتل: رفض الدنيا وما فيها والتماس ما عند الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq says if some night prayer escapes you, the day gives you free time; this is the sense of remembering your Lord’s name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r4.anchor: (وقال) (¬4) أبو إسحاق: أي (إن) (¬5) فاتك من الليل شيء، ذلك في النهار فراغ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r5.claim: Maqātil explains remembering the Lord’s name as affirming His oneness.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains tabattul as sincere devotion to God; Maqātil, al-Kalbī, Mujāhid, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk agree, as do all exegetes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أخلص إليه إخلاصا (¬9)، (وهو قول مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r7.claim: Qatāda specifies devoting worship and supplication to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: أخلص لله العبادة والدعوة (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r8.claim: Tabattul literally means cutting off; Mary is called al-Batūl because she turned away to worship, and a batla charity is severed from its owner’s property.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r8.anchor: وأصل معنى التبتل في اللغة: القطع (¬4)، (وقيل لمريم: البتول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r9.speaker: اللبث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r9.claim: Al-Layth says batl is separating one thing from another; al-batūl is a woman withdrawn from men, and tabattul can mean leaving marriage and renouncing it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r9.anchor: وقال اللبث: البتل: تمييز الشيء من الشىء، والبتول: كل امرأة تنقبض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r10.speaker: ربيعة بن مقروم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r10.claim: Rabīʿa ibn Maqrūm’s verse uses mutabattal for a monk devoted to worship and abstinent from marriage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r10.anchor: وقال (ربيعة) (¬2) بن مقروم (¬3): لو أنها عرضت لأشمط راهب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r11.claim: Abū Isḥāq glosses the command as withdrawing to God in worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r11.anchor: فقال أبو إسحاق: انقطع إليه في العبادة (¬6).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r12.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says a worshiper who leaves everything and turns to worship has cut off everything except God’s command and obedience; this amounts to sincerity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء: يقال للعابد إذا ترك كل شيء، وأقبل على العبادة: قد # تبتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r13.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r13.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam explains tabattul as rejecting the world and seeking what is with God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r13.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: التبتل: رفض الدنيا (¬2) وما فيها، والتماس (¬3) ما عند الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd says the command means devoting oneself to worship.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r15.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r15.claim: These explanations all return to withdrawing toward God and away from everything else.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r15.anchor: وهذا كله يرجع: (¬6) إلى معنى الانقطاع إليه عما سواه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r16.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r16.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r16.claim: Al-Akhfash notes that tabtīlan is not the direct verbal noun; the verbal noun is tabattul.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r16.anchor: وقال الأخفش في قوله: {وتبتل إليه تبتيلا} لم يجيء بمصدره، ومصدره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r17.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r17.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r17.claim: Others parse tabtīlan as a near-synonymous verbal noun, as if the wording were to cut oneself off to God; they compare 71:17, and this matches Abū Isḥāq’s semantic analysis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r17.anchor: وقال غيره (¬9): جاء تبتيلا على بتل نفسك إليه تبتيلا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494#2/r1.claim: Tabattal ilayhi means devote yourself wholly to Him; it derives from battalt al-shayʾ, to cut it off.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494#2/r1.anchor: {وتبتل إليه} أي انقطع إليه. من قولك: بتلت الشيء؛ إذا قطعته.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r7.claim: Remember the Lord's name by exalting and declaring Him transcendent.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r7.anchor: واذكر اسم ربك } بالتعظيم والتنزيه { وتبتل إليه تبتيلا } وانقطع إليه في العبادة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r8.claim: Tabattul means devoting oneself to God and separating oneself for worship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r8.anchor: وتبتل إليه تبتيلا } وانقطع إليه في العبادة. وقوله:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:8/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:8/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:8/r1.claim: Verses 1–7 prepare the Prophet inwardly to receive and internalize the divine message; these verses teach how to preach it and what to observe.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:8/r1.anchor: Önceki âyetler, ilâhî mesajı alarak onu kendi mânevî dünyasına yansıtması ve insanlara tebliğ etmesi için Hz. Peygamber’i psikolojik yönden hazırlamaya yönelikti. Bu âyetler ise mânevî hazırlıkla birlikte tebliğin nasıl yapılması ve nelere dikkat edilmesi gerektiğini öğretmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:8/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:8/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:8/r2.claim: The Prophet should continually remember God and seek His help, turn to Him sincerely, rely on His power, and trust His protection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:8/r2.anchor: daima Allah’ı anarak O’ndan yardım istemek, samimi kalp ile O’na yönelmek, O’nun gücüne dayanmak ve koruyuculuğuna güvenmek

BURHAN:v2p393/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p393/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p393/r3.claim: Although تبتيلا is not the regular verbal noun of تبتل, the verb is understood with the sense ‘detach yourself,’ which accounts for the form-II verbal noun.
BURHAN:v2p393/r3.anchor: واما قوله ﴿ وتبتل إليه تبتيلا ﴾ وان لم يكن جاريا على تبتل لكنه ضمن معنى بتل نفسك تبتلا

ITQAN:v3p178/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p178/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p178/r6.claim: Emphasis may use a verbal noun from another verb or a concrete noun instead of a verbal noun: “vegetation” means “growing.”
ITQAN:v3p178/r6.anchor: وقد يؤكد بمصدر فعل آخر أو اسم عين نيابة عن المصدر

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r13.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r13.claim: The verse pairs the form V verb tabattal with the form II verbal noun tabtīlan rather than the expected form V verbal noun tabattulan.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r13.anchor: وكان المتوقَّع أن يقول (وتبتل إليه تبتلاً) غير أنه لم يقل ذاك. وسبب ذلك أنه أراد أن يجمع بين مَعْنَيي التبتل والتبتيل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r14.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r14.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r14.claim: Form V conveys gradual, effortful progress, while form II conveys multiplication and intensity; using both captures both meanings concisely.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r14.anchor: فإن في تجسس وتحسس وبقية الأفعال تدرجاً وتكلفاً

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r15.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r15.claim: Examples such as kassar versus kasara and qattaʿa versus qataʿa show that form II can mark repeated or intensive action, unlike the basic form.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r15.anchor: وأما (فعّل) فيفيد التكثير والمبالغة وذلك نحو: كسر وكسّر، فإن في كسّر المضاعف من المبالغة والتكثير ما ليس في كَسَرَ الثلاثي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r16.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r16.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r16.claim: Tafsīr al-Qayyim explains that the verb supplies gradual effort and the verbal noun supplies intensification, so both commands are understood together.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r17.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r17.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r17.claim: The sequence is pedagogical: begin gradually in devotion, then build toward abundance; the verb conveys this developing stage and the verbal noun the enduring devotional state.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r17.anchor: الأصل أن يتدرج الإنسان من القلة إلى الكثرة، والمعنى: احمل نفسك على التبتل والانقطاع إلى الله في العبادة شيئاً فشيئاً حتى تصل إلى الكثرة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r1.claim: Instead of the expected verbal noun تبتل, the verse uses تبتيلاً from another form: تفعّل conveys gradual effort, while فعّل conveys multiplication and abundance.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r1.anchor: القياس أن يقال تبتّل تبتّلاً أنما في الآية جاء بالفعل ولم يأت بمصدره

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r2.claim: The wording teaches worshippers to begin with gradual, manageable devotion and then increase it, since steady progression leads to abundant worship.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r2.anchor: علّمنا تعالى أن نبدأ بالتدرج في العبادة شيئاً فشيئاً ثم ندخل في التكثير

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r3.claim: The verb form marks renewal and occurrence, while the nominal form marks stability, adding another deliberate rhetorical contrast.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r3.anchor: والتدرج والتكلف جاء بالصيغة الفعلية الدالة على الحدوث والتجدد (تبتّل) ثم جاء بالصيغة الإسمية الدالة على الثبوت

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r4.claim: Arabs grasped such eloquence naturally but could not produce this Qur'anic formulation, which the author presents as challenge and inimitability.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p114/r4.anchor: العرب قديماً كانوا يفهمون هذه البلاغة بالفطرة لكنهم عجزوا عن الإتيان بالصيغة التي جاء بها القرآن الكريم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r1.claim: Although the expected verbal noun is تبتّلاً, the verse pairs the fifth-form verb with a second-form verbal noun to combine the implications of both patterns.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r1.anchor: القياس أن يقال تبتّل تبتّلاً أنما في الآية جاء بالفعل ولم يأت بمصدره وإنما جاء بمصدر فعل آخر ليجمع بين أمرين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r2.claim: The fifth form conveys gradualness and effort; the second form conveys multiplication, as in breaking or cutting something into repeated pieces, so تبتيلاً adds intensification.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r2.anchor: صيغة تفعّل تفيد التدرج مثل تجرّع الماء أي جرعة جرعة وتحسّر فيها التدرج والتكلف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r3.claim: The wording teaches a gradual path in worship: begin with manageable devotion and increase toward abundant worship instead of taking on too much immediately.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r3.anchor: التبتّل هو الإنقطاع إلى الله في العبادة وقد علّمنا تعالى أن نبدأ بالتدرج في العبادة شيئاً فشيئاً ثم ندخل في التكثير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r4.claim: The verbal تبتّل signals a developing, renewed act, then the nominal تبتيلاً signals permanence, making the construction pedagogically deliberate.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r4.anchor: الدالة على الحدوث والتجدد (تبتّل) ثم جاء بالصيغة الإسمية الدالة على الثبوت (تبتيلا)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r5.claim: He calls the formulation a Quranic inimitability: Arabs grasped its rhetorical force instinctively but could not produce its form.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p563/r5.anchor: والعرب قديماً كانوا يفهمون هذه البلاغة بالفطرة لكنهم عجزوا عن الإتيان بالصيغة التي جاء بها القرآن الكريم
